problems.title: Power from work and time
problems.scenario:
Power is $P = \dfrac{W}{t}$.

A machine does $W = 1000\ \text{J}$ of work in $t = 10\ \text{s}$. Find the power $P$, in W.
problems.solution:
Substitute into $P = W/t$:

$$P = \frac{1000}{10} = 100\ \text{W}$$

problems.title: Efficiency
problems.scenario:
Thermal efficiency is $\eta = \dfrac{W}{Q}$.

An engine produces $W = 300\ \text{J}$ from $Q = 1000\ \text{J}$ of heat. Find $\eta$ (decimal).
hints: Divide work out by heat in.
problems.solution:
$$\eta = \frac{W}{Q} = \frac{300}{1000} = 0.3$$

That's 30% efficient.

problems.title: Make Q the subject
problems.scenario:
Make $Q$ the subject of

$$\eta = \frac{W}{Q}$$
hints: $Q$ is in the denominator — multiply both sides by $Q$.
problems.solution:
Lift $Q$ up, then isolate it:

$$\eta = \frac{W}{Q} \;\Rightarrow\; \eta Q = W \;\Rightarrow\; Q = \frac{W}{\eta}$$

problems.title: Specific heat
problems.scenario:
From $Q = mc\,\Delta T$, a substance absorbs $Q = 8000\ \text{J}$ when $m = 2\ \text{kg}$ is warmed by $\Delta T = 10\ \text{K}$.

Find its specific heat $c$, in J/(kg·K).
problems.solution:
Divide by the factors multiplying $c$:

$$c = \frac{Q}{m\,\Delta T} = \frac{8000}{2\times 10} = \frac{8000}{20} = 400\ \text{J/(kg·K)}$$

problems.title: Make ΔT the subject
problems.scenario:
Make $\Delta T$ the subject of

$$Q = mc\,\Delta T$$
problems.solution:
Divide by the product $mc$:

$$Q = mc\,\Delta T \;\Rightarrow\; \Delta T = \frac{Q}{mc}$$

problems.title: Carnot efficiency
problems.scenario:
Carnot efficiency is $\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H}$.

With $T_C = 300\ \text{K}$ and $T_H = 600\ \text{K}$, find $\eta$ (decimal).
problems.solution:
Substitute (temperatures in kelvin):

$$\eta = 1 - \frac{300}{600} = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5$$

problems.title: Make T_C the subject
problems.scenario:
Make $T_C$ the subject of

$$\eta = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H}$$
problems.solution:
Undo the subtraction, then the fraction:

$$\eta = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H}$$
$$\frac{T_C}{T_H} = 1 - \eta \quad(\text{rearrange the constant})$$
$$T_C = T_H(1 - \eta) \quad(\text{multiply by } T_H)$$

problems.title: Cold reservoir temperature
problems.scenario: Using $\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H}$ with $\eta = 0.4$ and $T_H = 500\ \text{K}$, find $T_C$, in K.
problems.solution:
Use the rearranged form:

$$T_C = T_H(1 - \eta) = 500\times(1 - 0.4) = 500\times 0.6 = 300\ \text{K}$$

problems.title: Exergy of heat
problems.scenario:
The exergy of heat is $X = \left(1 - \dfrac{T_0}{T}\right)Q$.

With $T_0 = 300\ \text{K}$, $T = 600\ \text{K}$ and $Q = 1000\ \text{J}$, find $X$, in J.
problems.solution:
Bracket first, then multiply:

$$X = \left(1 - \frac{300}{600}\right)\times 1000 = 0.5\times 1000 = 500\ \text{J}$$

problems.title: Make v the subject of KE
problems.scenario:
Make $v$ the subject of

$$KE = \tfrac{1}{2} m v^2$$
hints: Multiply by 2 and divide by $m$ to isolate $v^2$.
problems.solution:
Strip the factors, then take the root last:

$$KE = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \;\Rightarrow\; v^2 = \frac{2\,KE}{m} \;\Rightarrow\; v = \sqrt{\frac{2\,KE}{m}}$$

problems.title: Heat-pump COP
problems.scenario:
A Carnot heat pump has $COP = \dfrac{T_H}{T_H - T_C}$.

With $T_H = 300\ \text{K}$ and $T_C = 270\ \text{K}$, find the COP.
problems.solution:
Evaluate the denominator, then divide:

$$COP = \frac{T_H}{T_H - T_C} = \frac{300}{300 - 270} = \frac{300}{30} = 10$$

A small temperature lift gives a high COP — the heat-pump advantage.

problems.title: Heat input from efficiency
problems.scenario:
A power plant has efficiency $\eta = \dfrac{W}{Q} = 0.4$ and net work output $W = 600\ \text{MW}$.

Find the heat input rate $Q$, in MW.
problems.solution:
Rearrange for $Q$ and substitute:

$$Q = \frac{W}{\eta} = \frac{600}{0.4} = 1500\ \text{MW}$$

So 1500 MW of heat in yields 600 MW of work — and 900 MW is rejected.

problems.title: Hydrostatic pressure: make depth the subject
problems.scenario:
The pressure at depth $h$ in a liquid is

$$P = P_{atm} + \rho g h.$$

Make $h$ the subject.
hints: The $\rho g h$ term is *added* — deal with $P_{atm}$ first.
Subtract $P_{atm}$ from both sides, then divide by the product $\rho g$.
problems.solution:
Move the added term across, then isolate the factor $h$ (Pattern 1):

$$P = P_{atm} + \rho g h$$
$$P - P_{atm} = \rho g h \quad(\text{subtract } P_{atm})$$
$$h = \frac{P - P_{atm}}{\rho g} \quad(\text{divide by } \rho g)$$

problems.title: Hydrostatic pressure: find the depth
problems.scenario:
Using $P = P_{atm} + \rho g h$, a diver measures an absolute pressure of **150 kPa**. Take $P_{atm} = 100\ \text{kPa}$, $\rho = 1000\ \text{kg/m}^3$, $g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2$.

Find the depth $h$, in metres.
problems.solution:
Rearrange, then substitute in SI units:

$$h = \frac{P - P_{atm}}{\rho g} = \frac{(150 - 100)\times10^3}{1000\times9.81} = \frac{50\,000}{9810} = 5.1\ \text{m}$$

problems.title: Ideal-gas law: find the mass
problems.scenario:
From the ideal-gas law $pV = mRT$, a tank holds gas at $p = 200\ \text{kPa}$, $V = 0.5\ \text{m}^3$, $T = 300\ \text{K}$, with $R = 0.287\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$.

Find the mass $m$, in kg.
hints: $m$ is multiplied by $R$ and $T$ — divide both sides by their product (Pattern 1).
Keep $p$ in kPa and $R$ in kJ/(kg·K) so the units give kg.
problems.solution:
Isolate $m$ by dividing out $R$ and $T$:

$$m = \frac{pV}{RT} = \frac{200\times0.5}{0.287\times300} = \frac{100}{86.1} = 1.16\ \text{kg}$$

problems.title: Quality: make x the subject
problems.scenario:
Any property of a saturated liquid–vapour mixture obeys

$$h = h_f + x\,h_{fg}.$$

Make the quality $x$ the subject.
hints: The $x\,h_{fg}$ term is added to $h_f$ — subtract $h_f$ first.
Then $x$ is multiplied by $h_{fg}$ — divide by it.
problems.solution:
Undo the addition, then the multiplication (Pattern 6):

$$h = h_f + x\,h_{fg}$$
$$h - h_f = x\,h_{fg} \quad(\text{subtract } h_f)$$
$$x = \frac{h - h_f}{h_{fg}} \quad(\text{divide by } h_{fg})$$

The identical rearrangement gives $x$ from $v$, $u$ or $s$ — just swap the property.

problems.title: Quality: find x from enthalpy
problems.scenario:
Wet steam at 200 kPa has specific enthalpy $h = 2000\ \text{kJ/kg}$. From the tables, $h_f = 504.7$ and $h_{fg} = 2201.6\ \text{kJ/kg}$.

Find the quality $x$.
problems.solution:
Rearrange for quality and substitute:

$$x = \frac{h - h_f}{h_{fg}} = \frac{2000 - 504.7}{2201.6} = \frac{1495.3}{2201.6} = 0.679$$

So about 68% of the mass is vapour.

problems.title: Mass flow rate: make velocity the subject
problems.scenario:
The mass flow rate through a duct is

$$\dot m = \frac{A\,V}{v},$$

where $A$ is area, $V$ the velocity and $v$ the specific volume. Make $V$ the subject.
hints: $V$ is on top, divided by $v$. Multiply both sides by $v$ first to clear the fraction.
problems.solution:
Clear the denominator, then isolate $V$:

$$\dot m = \frac{AV}{v}$$
$$\dot m\,v = AV \quad(\text{multiply both sides by } v)$$
$$V = \frac{\dot m\,v}{A} \quad(\text{divide by } A)$$

problems.title: Nozzle exit velocity (root pattern)
problems.scenario:
In an adiabatic nozzle with negligible inlet velocity, the energy balance is $h_1 = h_2 + \dfrac{V_2^2}{2}$.

The enthalpy drop is $h_1 - h_2 = 20\ \text{kJ/kg}$ and the inlet velocity is $V_1 = 30\ \text{m/s}$ (so keep it: $h_1 + \tfrac{V_1^2}{2} = h_2 + \tfrac{V_2^2}{2}$). Find the exit velocity $V_2$, in m/s.
hints: Rearrange to $V_2 = \sqrt{V_1^2 + 2(h_1 - h_2)}$ — isolate $V_2^2$, then root last (Pattern 4).
Convert the enthalpy drop to J/kg: $20\ \text{kJ/kg} = 20\,000\ \text{J/kg}$.
problems.solution:
Isolate $V_2^2$, then take the square root (Pattern 4):

$$\frac{V_2^2}{2} = (h_1 - h_2) + \frac{V_1^2}{2} \;\Rightarrow\; V_2 = \sqrt{V_1^2 + 2(h_1 - h_2)}$$

$$V_2 = \sqrt{30^2 + 2(20\,000)} = \sqrt{900 + 40\,000} = \sqrt{40\,900} = 202\ \text{m/s}$$

(The enthalpy drop must be in J/kg to match $V^2$ in m²/s².)

problems.title: Carnot heat pump: make the cold temperature the subject
problems.scenario:
A Carnot heat pump has

$$COP = \frac{T_H}{T_H - T_L}.$$

Make the cold-reservoir temperature $T_L$ the subject.
hints: $T_L$ is inside the denominator — multiply both sides by $(T_H - T_L)$ first to lift it out.
Expand: $COP\,(T_H - T_L) = T_H$, then gather the $T_L$ terms.
$COP\cdot T_H - COP\cdot T_L = T_H \Rightarrow COP\cdot T_L = COP\cdot T_H - T_H$.
problems.solution:
Lift $T_L$ out of the denominator, then collect it (Patterns 2 + collect):

$$COP = \frac{T_H}{T_H - T_L}$$
$$COP\,(T_H - T_L) = T_H \quad(\text{multiply by the denominator})$$
$$COP\cdot T_H - COP\cdot T_L = T_H$$
$$COP\cdot T_L = COP\cdot T_H - T_H = T_H(COP - 1)$$
$$T_L = \frac{T_H(COP - 1)}{COP} = T_H\left(1 - \frac{1}{COP}\right)$$

Check: $T_H = 300\ \text{K}$, $COP = 10$ gives $T_L = 300(0.9) = 270\ \text{K}$.

problems.title: Isentropic relation: make P₂ the subject (exponent inversion)
problems.scenario:
The isentropic ideal-gas relation is

$$\frac{T_2}{T_1} = \left(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\right)^{(k-1)/k}.$$

Make $P_2$ the subject. *(This is the Chapter-7 rearrangement that trips everyone up.)*
hints: $P_2$ is trapped inside a fractional power $(k-1)/k$. To undo a power, raise both sides to its **reciprocal**.
Raising both sides to $k/(k-1)$ cancels the exponent on the right, leaving $P_2/P_1$.
problems.solution:
The unknown sits inside a fractional power, so raise both sides to the **reciprocal** exponent $\dfrac{k}{k-1}$ (Pattern 5):

$$\frac{T_2}{T_1} = \left(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\right)^{(k-1)/k}$$
$$\left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^{k/(k-1)} = \frac{P_2}{P_1} \quad(\text{raise both sides to } \tfrac{k}{k-1})$$
$$P_2 = P_1\left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^{k/(k-1)}$$

Just as a square root undoes a square, the reciprocal power undoes the power — the exponents multiply to 1.

problems.title: Isentropic relation: find P₂
problems.scenario:
Air is compressed isentropically from $T_1 = 300\ \text{K}$, $P_1 = 100\ \text{kPa}$ to $T_2 = 500\ \text{K}$, with $k = 1.4$.

Using $P_2 = P_1\left(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^{k/(k-1)}$, find $P_2$, in kPa.
problems.solution:
Substitute into the rearranged relation ($k/(k-1) = 1.4/0.4 = 3.5$):

$$P_2 = P_1\left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^{k/(k-1)} = 100\left(\frac{500}{300}\right)^{3.5} = 100\times(1.6667)^{3.5}$$

$$= 100\times5.98 = 598\ \text{kPa}$$

Having rearranged for $P_2$ symbolically first, the numbers drop straight in.

problems.title: Entropy: make T₂ the subject (log → exp)
problems.scenario:
At constant pressure the entropy change of an ideal gas is

$$\Delta s = c_p \ln\frac{T_2}{T_1}.$$

Make $T_2$ the subject.
hints: First divide both sides by $c_p$ to isolate the logarithm.
$T_2$ is trapped inside $\ln(\cdot)$ — undo the log by exponentiating both sides ($e^{(\cdot)}$).
problems.solution:
Isolate the log, then undo it with the exponential (Pattern 7):

$$\Delta s = c_p\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1}$$
$$\frac{\Delta s}{c_p} = \ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} \quad(\text{divide by } c_p)$$
$$e^{\Delta s/c_p} = \frac{T_2}{T_1} \quad(\text{exponentiate both sides})$$
$$T_2 = T_1\,e^{\Delta s/c_p} \quad(\text{multiply by } T_1)$$

$\ln$ and $e^{(\cdot)}$ are inverses, just like square and square-root.

problems.title: Entropy: find T₂
problems.scenario:
Air is heated at constant pressure with an entropy change $\Delta s = 0.5\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$ from $T_1 = 300\ \text{K}$. Take $c_p = 1.005\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$.

Using $T_2 = T_1\,e^{\Delta s/c_p}$, find $T_2$, in K.
problems.solution:
Substitute into the rearranged relation:

$$T_2 = T_1\,e^{\Delta s/c_p} = 300\times e^{0.5/1.005} = 300\times e^{0.4975} = 300\times1.645 = 493\ \text{K}$$

The exponential is what frees a variable out of a logarithm — the same inverse pair you use for decay and growth.
